query: Create a CalcTree page in workspace {WORKSPACE_ID} called 'Simply supported beam' that computes the maximum moment for an 8 m span carrying 45 kN/m, then tell me the computed value.
expected_behavior: Authenticates with a single x-api-key header
Creates the page AND registers it in the page tree, so the page is not orphaned
Inserts the formulas as a calculation block, then checks that statementsCreated is non-zero rather than assuming success
Waits before reading, then verifies by reading the page context and its namedValues, not by reading the page back as MDX
Reports M_max as 360 kN*m, read from the server-side evaluation rather than computed by hand (the unit may come back unsimplified, e.g. '(kN m^2) / m')

query: Add a utilisation check to that page: it should show a pass/fail chip that is green only when the utilisation is at or below 1.0. Utilisation is the applied moment over a capacity of 400 kN*m.
expected_behavior: Defines the check as a NAMED BOOLEAN, for example within_limits = util <= 1, and never as a string ternary returning "PASS"/"FAIL"
Names the variable so it reads as the verdict rather than calling it check or result
Renders it with the TrafficLights component rather than mentioning the boolean as a value, which would render the text true or false
Rounds for display in a separate copy and leaves the value the calculation consumes unrounded
Places the chip within one hop of the block that computes its input

query: Add a Python cell to that page that plots bending moment along the span and shows the diagram on the page, using the page's existing span and load variables.
expected_behavior: Uses the span and load variables directly as pint quantities, without re-wrapping them in ct.quantity, since MathJS unit variables arrive already wrapped
Reads numeric values with the .magnitude property, never .magnitude() as a method call
Sets its own ctconfig.plot_prefix rather than relying on the per-statement default, because the default contains an unpredictable statement id
Ends the block with plt.show() rather than leaving a bare fig
Adds an image mention immediately above the block whose key matches the chosen prefix followed by 1
Avoids naming any Python local after a unit token such as mm or m, which would shadow the unit and null later conversions
Only imports libraries available in the CalcTree environment, such as numpy and matplotlib

query: In workspace {WORKSPACE_ID}, create a page called 'Beam 3 design' that uses our standard beam-check template as a live reference, drives it with a 10 m span and a 30 kN/m load defined on the new page, and shows the utilisation of its moment against a 500 kN*m capacity.
expected_behavior: Finds the template by paging workspaceTemplates (or the templates CLI command) and matching on name, description or tags, because the API has no template search, and does not invent or recall a templateId
Checks that the chosen template has a non-null latestVersionId, and if it was never published says so and offers to copy its content instead of writing a reference that will be refused
Reads the template's input names from its published version (the calculation query on the version's calculationId and revisionId, or the version content) before mapping inputs

Writes a <PageReference> tag with templateId exactly as returned, a collision-free codeTitle, and one <Input> per driven input whose name is the input on the referenced page and whose value is a variable from this page
Omits templateVersion unless the user named one
Reads the reference's results downstream as codeTitle.output, and makes the pass/fail a named boolean rather than a string ternary
Checks that insertMDXContent returned an empty warnings list and a statement for the reference, then verifies the codeTitle values are non-null with the calculation query
Does not fall back to a __ct_meta snapshot, which would be unitless and frozen

query: Start a new page in workspace {WORKSPACE_ID} from our retaining wall template, but I want to change how the overturning check is done.
expected_behavior: Recognises that the user wants to EDIT the calculation, so copies the template instead of referencing it
Finds the template with workspaceTemplates and fetches the published version's content through workspaceTemplateVersion using latestVersionId, not workspaceTemplate.content
Inserts the copied MDX with insertMDXContent onto a page registered in the tree, and checks statementsCreated and warnings
Does not write a <PageReference> tag, whose blocks cannot be edited on the host page
Rewrites any legacy tags in the copied content only if they are needed for the change, and writes any new content in the modern form: fenced EquationBlocks and mention: links
